jobs.title: Sales Development Representative at Inner Peak
jobs.description: Employer: Inner Peak Expires: 09/27/2026 This position is ideal for a recent college graduate looking for their first sales role or a college student looking to earn a little extra money and gain valuable experience. We are a lean team trying to keep costs low. This role is compensated solely based on results - you will be paid per meeting you book for our CEO, as well as a percentage of any deal that closes. There is no base salary, and we have no flexibility on this. If you are not comfortable working on commission only, please do not apply. Summary: Inner Peak AI (www.innerpeak.ai) is blending new AI technology with human therapist expertise to deliver truly personalized, affordable mental wellness support 24/7. We are starting by serving high school and college students but eventually intend to be everyone’s mental wellness safety net, triaging users and delivering them to video content, human therapists, or crisis resources. We are a mission-driven company created out of our founders; own lived experience and struggles with mental health, and are still a small (but motivated) team. Peak’s founders met in undergrad at Harvard a decade ago before reconnecting recently over their shared interest in technology and mental health. We have built and launched a mobile application that has two thousand users and is live at several high schools. Initial student usage data is strong, giving us powerful case studies. To raise our next round of fundraising, we must scale this to more schools. We are looking for hungry interns who care about making a difference in peer mental health and who want high-upside potential through our performance-based compensation. This role is great training for anyone interested in going into sales, as you will report to a sales manager with 10+ years of sales experience. If you are successful at this role, over time it could turn into a full account executive role with a base salary. Responsibilities:You will be acting as a lead-generation sales representative for Inner Peak, talking to real potential customersYou will be calling private and charter school principals, deans of students, directors of counseling, and counselorsYou will learn to use Hubspot, the top startup CRMYour primary goal is to generate interest in Inner Peak’s solution so school leaders will want to see a demo of Inner PeakYour success will be measured in number of meetings booked for our CEO Qualifications:Preference for past sales experience - at minimum you must WANT to sellNo requirement for past sales experience (though it could help), but you have to WANT to sellYou must be personable, friendly, and not intimidated by cold callingInterest in / passion for mental health and / or K-12 educationHard-working, with the ability to put your head down and do callsA self-starter looking to bet on yourself You must be able to devote at least 10 hours a week during normal business hours to the role (though preference for candidates who can devote more)

jobs.title: Project Engineer Intern at Murray Company
jobs.description: Employer: Murray Company Expires: 09/27/2026 Come grow with us...At Murray Company, how we operate is defined by shared values that are 100 years in the making - Safety, Quality, Honesty, Hard Work and Pride of Ownership. These values have led to our company consistently being in the top 15% on ENRs Best Specialty Contractor’s list. Bring your enthusiasm and unique perspective to Murray Company where you will have the opportunity to grow with us professionally, personally, and financially. Join a team that cares about helping you thrive and succeed. You'll work alongside talented colleagues while establishing lifelong friendships and making a difference in our company and the specialty contracting community. Position SummaryAre you a current student looking to expand your knowledge and business acumen with practical hands-on experience and training opportunities? Start your career with a summer internship at Murray Company, - one of the nation’s Top 20 Mechanical Contractors and a leader in innovation and excellence. As an intern in our Operations group reporting to our talented project managers, you will work alongside our top-notch teams in our pre-construction, fabrication and field installation functions. This internship offers the opportunity to gain hands-on Project Management experience in support of mechanical projects of various sizes and specialties (plumbing, HVAC, process piping, and industrial). Location: Cypress or Rancho Dominguez, CA, with anticipated travel to designated project sites in and around the Southern California metropolitan area. Compensation: $26.00 per hour Internship Program Schedule & HoursDuration: 40 hours per week for 10-12 consecutive weeks, beginning as early as May 2027.Typical working hours are Monday to Friday, 7 am - 4 pm (subject to change depending on local project requirements).Program participants must be available to work within the required schedule for the duration of the internship. Key ResponsibilitiesAssist in planning, scheduling, and coordinating mechanical projects.Provide support for reviewing designs, drawings, and specifications.Assist with managing project documentation, including submittals, RFIs, change orders, and reports.Participate in site visits to monitor progress and ensure compliance with specifications.Support the preparation of cost estimates and budgets.Aid in the implementation of quality control measures.Facilitate communication among project teams, subcontractors, suppliers, and clients.Assist with safety protocol implementation and compliance. QualificationsRequiredMust be currently enrolled in an accredited university program and actively pursuing a degree in Construction Management, Mechanical Engineering or related field.Proficiency in computer programs such as Microsoft Office Products (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, etc.).Demonstrated ability to take initiative and interact effectively in a team environment.Availability to work 40 hours per week within the required schedule for the duration of the internship (typically 10 weeks).PreferredStrong organizational skills.Ability to multi-task and work in a fast-paced environment.Experience with construction software such as Revit, Navisworks, Bluebeam, Procore, ACC Build or other related programs. Physical RequirementsProlonged periods of sitting at a desk.Must be able to lift to 15 pounds at times.Must have sufficient visual acuity to view and interpret detailed construction drawings on computer screens and on paper.Must be able to traverse uneven surfaces on project sites and climb stairs to access project site temporary offices. Contingent EmploymentOffers of employment are contingent upon successful completion of the Company’s required pre-employment drug screening process. Murray Company is a federal contractor and complies with all applicable federal laws and regulations regarding controlled substances. Work AuthorizationMurray Company is not sponsoring employment-based visas at this time. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on an ongoing, permanent basis without the need for current or future visa sponsorship.

jobs.title: Field Intern at Dr. Kim Schrier's Congressional Campaign
jobs.description: Employer: Dr. Kim Schrier's Congressional Campaign Expires: 09/27/2026 Dr. Kim Schrier for Congress seeks a Field Intern for the 2026 election. The Field Intern will be responsible for supporting canvassing efforts in the 8th Congressional District and attending events with the Congresswoman and will play a critical role in community outreach. This position requires 12-15 hours a week, primarily in the evenings and weekends for voter contact. A regular week may include direct voter contact during weekday evenings and attending a parade or canvass launch on weekend mornings. The desired start date is September 15th, 2026 and an end date of November 3rd, 2026. The position pays $17.13 per hour with mileage reimbursement. The person in this position will be expected to work irregular hours, including evenings and weekends, and must have access to a laptop, internet, and a reliable car. The Field Intern will report to the Field Organizer. Job ResponsibilitiesWorking alongside the Field Organizer, volunteers, and other supporters on direct voter contact efforts including: phone banking, canvassing, text banking, and paradesCoordinating regular direct voter contact activities Coordinating yard sign distributionMeeting personal goals for phone calls, door knocking, and yard signs — averaging 200-250 doors knocked per weekRepresenting the campaign at events throughout the districtOther duties as assigned Skills and ExperienceSelf-motivated and self-startingAble to perform and thrive in high stress environmentsAble to prioritize multiple deadlines and handle regular challenges with a positive attitudeAble to work inclusively and collaborativelyExcellent written and verbal communication skills and an ability to communicate proactivelyAble to manage projects independently Job LocationThe position will be based in Issaquah, WA with travel throughout the 10,000 square mile district expected! To ApplyDo not apply through the Handshake platform. Please send a resume to info@drkimschrier.com with the subject line “Field Intern Application.” The position will remain open until filled. The start date for this position will be September 15th. Dr. Kim Schrier for Congress provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics.

In addition to our expert styling, we offer personalized consultations and a curated selection of retail products to empower our clients to embrace and care for their unique hair journey. Committed to fostering a sense of community and empowerment, we also host local events that celebrate diversity and promote the normalization of natural hair in every facet of life, from professional to personal to luxurious. At Thrive Hair Bar, we believe in the transformative power of embracing one’s natural beauty, and we are dedicated to helping our clients feel confident, empowered and utterly fabulous in their natural glory.Internship ResponsibilitiesThis role expectations are that you dedicate at least 8 hours per week to Thrive Hair Bar assignments which are due 1x per week, attend weekly one on ones with the CEO, and work in person at least 1x per week for a minimum of 2 hours. Some assignments require in-person work and some assignments can be done remotely.The responsibilities include creating & editing marketing materials including emails, social media posts, website posts, videos, an internal newsletter, the marketing calendar and recruiting model talent.Internship BenefitsWork closely with a startup CEO from Columbia and UPENNsee behind the scenes of what launching a new company from the ground up is like$100 monthly stipend1 free hair appointment per monthand you are invited to all Thrive Hair Bar team activities!Submission GuidelinesPlease submit 4 items: 1. Cover Letter in PDF Format, 2. Writing Sample (this can be something you created in the past/for a class) in PDF OR JPG FORMAT, 3. Social Media Post/Video/ReelSample (something with imagery) YOU CAN LINK TO YOUR INSTAGRAM OR SEND A PDF OR JPG IMAGE/POST, 4. Resume in PDF format

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Project Engineer Intern- Raleigh, NC at SteelFab, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: SteelFab, Inc. Expires: 10/01/2026 As a Project Engineer Intern at SteelFab, you’ll work closely with our Preconstruction and Project Management teams. You’ll take on responsibilities that will enhance your skills and prepare you for a successful career in the steel construction industry. *This is an office-based position. Primary job duties will not be on project sites or manufacturing environments. Key Responsibilities: Preconstruction Gather subcontractor pricing for new project estimates. Review and analyze subcontractor bids to ensure alignment with project specifications. Perform detailed material and labor take-offs. Prepare pricing recaps for senior leadership. Visit job sites to see job progress and build relationships with clients and vendors Fabrication Shop Experience: Gain hands-on experience with the fabrication flow and production processes to deepen your understanding of the steel construction lifecycle. Project Management Project Management duties will be based on project schedules. Example duties: Draft and issue purchase orders and subcontracts to vendors. Evaluate design drawing revisions to identify and manage scope changes effectively. Manage the coordination of construction drawings and models and review submittals. Collaborate with onsite subcontractors to identify and resolve field issues. Why SteelFab? SteelFab is the nation's largest structural steel fabricator and a proud third-generation family-owned business. When you join us, you become part of a tradition of excellence and innovation in the construction industry. Our interns benefit from: Hands-on experience and mentorship from industry professionals. Clear paths for advancement within SteelFab and opportunities to shape your career. Building relationships with teammates, vendors, and industry leaders. SteelFab’s commitment to fairness, reliability, and ethical practices. Desired Candidate Attributes We are looking for Project Engineer Interns who embody the values and qualities that drive SteelFab’s success. Ideal candidates will demonstrate: A passionate and energetic approach to problem-solving and customer satisfaction. The ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment. An eagerness to learn, enthusiasm for the industry, and a desire for personal and professional growth. A team-first mentality, prioritizing collective success over individual achievement. Reliability and dependability Career Progression: Project Engineer Intern Project Engineer Assistant Project Manager or Estimator Project Manager (if previously APM) Senior PM or Senior Estimator Qualifications and Requirements Major: Engineering, Construction Management, or related fields Required: Microsoft Office experience, common computer skills. Valid driver’s license Preferred: Some experience in the construction or engineering industry through work, internships, or part-time employment.

jobs.title: Media Specialist at Camp Bear Creek
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Bear Creek Expires: 10/02/2026 Media Specialist – Summer StaffLocation: Camp Bear Creek – Eastern IowaWebsite: https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/Dates: May 23-July 24, 2027Camp Bear Creek is a Christian summer camp in Eastern Iowa serving kids from kindergarten through 12th grade. We’re looking for passionate, fun, dedicated people who want to spend a summer making a real difference — in the lives of campers and in their own.Come work as a Media Specialist at Camp Bear Creek. We are seeking a talented individual who is ready to put their skills into practice. The Media Specialist for the summer gains a lot of experience in, well, all things media. However, you also have the chance to do a lot more than that. You'll be immersed in the summer camp environment, interacting with children and youth in a Christian setting, learning how to capture their stories and how to share the mission of the camp, the joy of the moment, and the magic of summer in something as simple as a photograph or as complex as a ten minute video.The Media Specialist is responsible for camp photography and videography. You'll be out there with the camera, whether it's a DSLR or the GoPro, capturing that kid's giant smile as they go flying down the slip 'n slide or the moment they make it to the top of the rock wall or their splash landing at the bottom of the mud slide. The Media Specialist maintains the daily summer camp blog, which parents depend on as one of their only sources of communication with their child while they're away for six days at camp. They want to know what it feels like to be at camp even when they can't be there themselves, and the best Media Specialist will be able to help them do that. The Media Specialist updates the camp social media accounts, engaging a diverse community of all ages and experiences that spans back over a 65 year history. The Media Specialist designs a weekly summary video, compiling everything that they have captured during the week and uniquely putting it all together into an 8-10 minute video that parents and campers will not only watch over and over, but they'll want to show others because it so perfectly captures what camp was like.If you think you're ready for a summer like this and to be the Media Specialist, please complete the application through the camp’s website at https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/ You'll walk away from the summer with a bigger portfolio, college credit, and a wealth of experience. Plus, you can't discount the chance to have some fun at camp, either!

jobs.description: Employer: Confluence Environmental Center, AmeriCorps Program Expires: 10/07/2026 Dates of Service October 21st, 2026 – July 29th, 2027 (1,200 hours, approx. 32 hours/week) POSITION TITLEDepave for Trees Coordinator Project PARTNEROregon Walks and Depavehttps://oregonwalks.org/https://www.depave.org/ Position SummaryThis position is in partnership between the Confluence Environmental Center, AmeriCorps Program, DePave and Oregon Walks. 82nd Avenue is in the middle of major public reinvestment, and one of the clearest calls from the community has been for less pavement and more green space, especially trees. This position exists to answer that call on the ground: designing a new "micro-depaving" pilot program that partners directly with private landowners to remove small sections of pavement, plant a tree, and support the landowner in maintaining it. This position will build the relationships and evidence base for a micro-depaving program model through community outreach, education, and partnership building to support increased access to greenspaces along 82nd Avenue.Estimated time breakdown: 40% research, pilot program design; 30% outreach, recruitment, and education; up to 10% project fundraising; and 20% Confluence cohort/leadership development activities. The AmeriCorps Volunteer will participate in Confluence-led leadership development activities which include: Leadership Development Training Series, team meetings, National Service events and other self-directed development opportunities (20%). Essential Functions (to include, but not limited to):Research and design a "micro-depaving" program model for small-scale private-lot depaving projects along the 82nd Avenue corridor including explanations on how to identify sites, how to engage with land owners, how to navigate permitting, and how to contract with partners.Outreach to private landowners along 82nd Avenue to identify potential participantsBuild and maintain relationships with community and technical partners, including the 82nd Avenue Coalition, BRANCH Coalition partners, the City of Portland, and local workforce development organizations.Coordinate with City of Portland permitting staff to understand how the program design stays within permit-exempt thresholds.Identify and define project metrics, outcomes, and narratives to support project sustainability including information about the history of over paving, its impacts on the community, and the importance of depaving and tree canopy development.Complete and submit all necessary paperwork and reports in a timely manner; attend and complete all training and service requirements; wear Confluence uniform and/or appropriate identifiers and required safety gear while performing service or attending official events.Abide by program and AmeriCorps policies. Under no circumstances will AmeriCorps Volunteers be asked to perform prohibited activities outlined in the approved grant. Position RequirementsDeep interest in environmental justice, urban forestry, and environmental work.Comfortable engaging directly with private landowners and community members from a wide range of backgrounds; lived experience in community organizing or outreach is valued equally with formal education.Written and verbal communication skills to draft outreach materials, meeting notes, and grant application materials (specific grant-writing experience is not required but is a benefit).Regular and reliable attendance and dependability; ability to serve as part of a team spanning two host organizations.Willingness/openness to learn about and discuss racial equity and social justice issues.Regular and reliable attendance and dependability. AmeriCorps Volunteers must be: 17 years of age or older at beginning of service term; U.S. citizen, national or lawful permanent resident; in possession of a high school diploma or equivalent, or commit to earning one prior to receiving education award; able to commit to the full term of service; able to successfully pass a fingerprint criminal history background check and satisfactory report from the National Sex Offender Public Website (NSOPW) prior to the start of the position.Ability to serve as part of a diverse team. Preferred QualificationsBilingual or multilingual skills relevant to 82nd Avenue's communities (e.g., Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese).Experience or coursework in urban forestry, landscape design, environmental science, or a related field.Familiarity with East Portland or the 82nd Avenue corridor.Experience with data tracking tools (Excel, Google Sheets) or basic GIS/mapping.Experience organizing or facilitating community events or volunteer work. Member Benefits Include$15,200 living allowance paid over the 8-month term of service (approx. $1,688 monthly, before taxes). $5,176 education award (qualified student loans and/or education expenses) Loan Forbearance Health Care InsuranceChild Care Reimbursement Option$50 Training Fund Professional Leadership Certificate, Trainings and Networking opportunities. May be eligible for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).Monthly TriMet passes available.Access to a Member Assistance Program (free counseling, health & financial tips, etc.)Access to a large network of partner organizationsAccess to events, networking, professional development, and conferencesThe knowledge that you’re working on important environmental justice issues facing tens of thousands of folks in east Portland Project Location & Transportation InformationMember’s office space will be at Depave's Portland office located at River Street Studios (820 N River St, Portland OR) in Portland's inner east side. In person organizing/canvassing and site visits will largely occur on/near 82nd Avenue.Portland has a robust public transit network between the office space and 82nd Avenue. The member is encouraged to utilize public transportation and bicycle transportation. Trimet but and Max routes can be found here.

Why this could be a fit for you This could be a fit for you if you’re interested in how organizations operate behind the scenes and enjoy bringing structure, coordination, and problem-solving to complex work. It’s an opportunity to build broad business exposure, strengthen your professional skills, and contribute to work that helps teams execute more effectively across the organization. Summer Internship Program The BNY Summer Internship Program offers high-potential students a dynamic 10-week experience designed to accelerate development, build professional networks, and provide meaningful exposure to one of the world's leading financial services institutions. Through a skills-driven talent model, interns gain insight into the capabilities, platforms, and functions that power BNY's global franchise while contributing to impactful business initiatives. From day one, interns are immersed in BNY's collaborative and innovative culture through: Enterprise-wide onboarding and development programming, including an in person immersive induction experience, executive speaker series, skill development, and networking opportunities. Meaningful project work aligned to key business practices and platforms, providing hands-on experience, skill development, and real-world business impact. Structured mentorship and career support from managers, senior leaders, peer mentors, business stakeholders, and dedicated program managers. Exposure across practices, platforms, and teams, building a broad understanding of BNY's integrated business model. Professional, technical, and financial services training designed to strengthen business acumen and prepare participants for long-term career success. A premier early-career experience, backed by senior leadership and designed to develop the next generation of talent for BNY's global workforce. jobs.description: Employer: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture Expires: 10/09/2026 NOTE: Applications submitted through Handshake will NOT be considered.Interpretative Research and Programs InternshipHybrid Part-Time Internship and Hybrid Full-Time Internship$425/week and $850/weekJanuary 25 – April 23, 2027Desired Majors and Areas of Study: Museum Studies, Museum Education, African American Studies, Africana/African Diaspora Studies and History, Latin American and Caribbean History, American Studies, Public History, Performance Studies; All encouraged to applyThe Office of Strategic Partnerships (OSP) exists to strengthen the capabilities and sustainability of historical, cultural, and art institutions focused on African American and African Diaspora, which we do through our collaborations with museum service organizations, professional associations, and related organizations.Through collaboration and partnerships, OSP:• Delivers far-reaching and transformative support for under-resourced organizations on a regional, national, and international level;• Connects and builds awareness about the work of its participating institutions;• Provides access to training and resources that support and advance leaders and field-wide best practices.The Interpretative Research and Programs Intern will support the continued development and relaunch of the Ethical Interpretation Workshop, a signature program of the National Museum of African American History and Culture (NMAAHC)/OSP. While ethical interpretation is embedded throughout the Museum’s collections, digital platforms, and exhibitions, no single exhibition exclusively focuses on this topic. This internship will play a key role in advancing both a Smithsonian-wide pilot program and a national workshop dedicated to ethical theory and practice, with particular emphasis on illustrating the historical and contemporary relationships between African American communities and the natural world.The selected intern will contribute to the planning, coordination, and preparation of materials for these initiatives, with primary responsibilities centered on research and administrative support. As time permits, the intern may also assist in organizing and facilitating virtual or in-person professional development programs and meetups for the growing Community of Practice focused on ethical interpretation. The intern will join the planning teams for these efforts and support the development of program-related resources and communications.The project will enable the intern to:Gain hands-on experience in planning, coordinating, and developing program materials for the Smithsonian-wide pilot program and national Ethical Interpretation Workshop;Develop a deep understanding of ethical interpretation theory and practice, particularly as it relates to African American and African Diasporic communities and their relationships with the natural world;Conduct object-specific and biographical research to support workshops, and program development;Build skills in interpreting material culture and historical narratives in ways that are accessible and meaningful to a broad, diverse audience, particularly those interested in African American art, history, and culture;Learn to distill large quantities of multimedia exhibition content into thematic, succinct, and engaging museum tours;Gain insight into exhibition rotation cycles, object display length, and the multidisciplinary nature of museum exhibitions and interpretation;Develop object interpretation, public speaking, storytelling, and audience engagement skills;Meet one-on-one with professionals across the museum and broader cultural sector to explore career paths, professional development, and sector-specific opportunities.Through this internship, the intern will gain exposure to the external-facing work of OSP; the national landscape of interpretive practice; models for presenting sensitive historical content; the relationship between interpretation and tourism; and strategies for partnership development, strategic planning, and problem solving. The experience may include site visits to African American museums, universities, and sites of memory throughout the Washington, D.C. metro area, as well as travel to the Association of African American Museums Annual Conference.The ideal candidate will have some knowledge/appreciation for African American History and Public History, experience with partnership development/outreach, and research, and excellent writing and communication skills.Internship Duties Include (but are not limited to):Participate in an online review and physical walkthrough of all museum exhibition galleries with OSP Staff, and other NMAAHC curators, as availableResearch effective methods of program facilitation and audience engagement techniquesIdentify and research key objects on view in NMAAHC exhibitions that fit within the scope and intended content of this projectDevelop a Smithsonian wide exhibition guide centered around ethical interpretation specifically focusing on the narratives of Africans/African AmericansCreate a presentation and/or talking points for each exhibition guide that can be used by other NMAAHC curators, docents, and museum staff on OSP-centered toursUnderstand how to effectively use multiple interpretative methodologies to create impactful public programs, utilizing audience engagement techniquesObserve Museum leadership and strategic planning initiativesAttend virtual cross-departmental meetings, workshops, and special events

jobs.title: Undergraduate Music and Performing Arts Curatorial Internship at Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture
jobs.description: Employer: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture Expires: 10/09/2026 NOTE: Applications submitted through Handshake will NOT be considered.Undergraduate Music and Performing Arts Curatorial InternshipPart-Time Hybrid Internship$425/weekJanuary 25 – April 23, 2027Desired Majors and Areas of Study: Museum Studies, Music, Film, Television, Theater History and/or Performance Studies, American historyThis internship is an opportunity to do meaningful curatorial work at one of the most prominent cultural institutions in the country building skills in African American collecting and cultural preservation while expanding professional networks. As part of NMAAHC’s commitment to strengthening the museum talent pipeline, this position is designed to support undergraduate students in gaining foundational knowledge and hands-on experience, while introducing them to the many different career paths that curatorial work can open. The skills developed through this internship (research, writing, object documentation, and professional communication) directly support careers across a wide range of museum positions, including curatorial, collections, education, public programs, and outreach, as well as related fields such as archival work, cultural policy, and the broader nonprofit and public humanities sectors. By the end of the internship the intern will be able to: Navigate and use the TMS (The Museum System) collection information database to locate and support documentation of collection records;Assist with the handling and processing of objects and archival materials following professional conservation and preservation standards;Assist with the creation and review of collection inventories, contributing to the Museum’s collections stewardship goals;Support object research and assist with producing accurate collection documentation as directed by the curator;Research and prepare donor briefs and profiles that support the curator’s donor cultivation and community stewardship efforts;Assist with drafting and editing collection and exhibition texts;Assist with drafting object acquisition proposals using curatorial criteria and an understanding of the museum’s collecting priorities;Produce interpretive labels and an exhibition narrative for a proposed exhibition drawn from the NMAAHC Music & Performing Arts Collection, with support from the curator;Research and write an acquisition proposal with curatorial guidance and present it to the NMAAHC Collections Committee; Develop an understanding of museums as institutions of cultural stewardship and gain insight into the importance of collecting and preservation through direct engagement with the collection and curatorial practice.The Office of Curatorial Affairs advances NMAAHC’s mission of sharing the history and culture of African Americans and all people of African descent with a diverse public by collecting, preserving, researching, and interpreting artifacts of lasting cultural significance. The Music and Performing Arts Curator contributes to this mission by stewarding a collection that spans the full breadth of African American creative expression (including music, television, film, theater, dance, comedy, and popular culture) from everyday creative life to landmark performances, recordings, and cultural movements. All of these areas are available to the intern. As an undergraduate intern, you will assist the curator with collections acquisition and processing, object documentation, research, and writing, supporting an active list of ongoing projects throughout the internship. Before your start date, you will be given a list of Music and Performing Arts collections to select which collection(s) you want to focus on, allowing you to align the experience with your academic interests and professional goals. This internship will strengthen your research and writing skills, expand your professional network across the museum, and give you a clearer sense of the many directions a career in curatorial work can take.This is a hybrid internship, combining remote work with scheduled onsite days at NMAAHC in Washington, DC, and a storage facility in Maryland. Start and end dates are to be determined in coordination with the intern and supervisor.The ideal candidate is an undergraduate student or recent graduate with coursework or a demonstrated interest in African American history and culture, with a focus on music, performing arts, popular culture, or museum studies. A genuine curiosity about Black history and culture and its relationship to music and the performing arts is essential. An interest in developing research and writing skills in a museum setting is important. Prior experience with curatorial or archival work is a plus but not required. Comfort with word processing and spreadsheet software is expected; experience with collection management systems is welcome but not necessary.The internship includes two projects developed with curatorial guidance:The first is a proposed exhibition of your choice drawn from the NMAAHC Music & Performing Arts Collection. With support from the curator, you will select objects and images, conduct research, develop an exhibition narrative, and write interpretive labels resulting in a portfolio piece and writing sample that reflects the full arc of your internship experience.The second is an acquisition proposal. With guidance from the curator, you will research and write a proposal for an object or collection of your choice (which may include contemporary materials that document living artists, emerging genres, or current cultural events) and present it to the NMAAHC Collections Committee.Duties Include (but are not limited to):Attend curatorial team meetings to observe institutional processes and build familiarity with museum operationsDevelop familiarity with the TMS (The Museum System) collection information database to locate documentation of collection recordsAssist with the handling and documentation of objects and archival materials following professional conservation and preservation standardsAssist with the creation and review of collection inventoriesSupport object research and assist with producing accurate collection documentation as directed by the curatorResearch and prepare briefs and profiles for the curator’s visits with potential donorsAssist with drafting and editing collection and exhibition textsAssist with drafting object acquisition proposals in support of ongoing collections workWrite interpretive labels and supporting materials for the exhibition projectResearch and write an acquisition proposal with curatorial guidance and present it to the NMAAHC Collections Committee

jobs.description: Employer: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture Expires: 10/09/2026 NOTE: Applications submitted through Handshake will NOT be considered.Council Oral History Project InternshipHybrid Part-Time Internship$425/weekJanuary 25 – April 19, 2027Desired Majors and Areas of Study: Oral History, Public History, Library Science, Archival Management, Museum Studies, Arts Management, African American History and Cultural Studies, Cultural Heritage and Preservation, Digital Preservation and Records Management, Museum Collections and Collections Management, Nonprofit Leadership and Philanthropy Studies, Archival Research and Information ManagementThe Office of the Director is responsible for guiding the museum’s operation and mission. In coordination with the NMAAHC staff and Council, the Office of the Director oversees the preservation, documentation, display, and dissemination of African American history and culture to a diverse and global audience. The Council Oral History Project Internship provides hands-on experience supporting the preservation and documentation of the history of the National Museum of African American History and Culture (NMAAHC). The internship is a collaborative opportunity between the Office of the Director's Council Relations and Museum Initiatives team and the Oral History Initiative within the Office of Digital Strategies and Engagement. The project focuses on collecting, preserving, and organizing the oral histories of Founding Council members who played a significant role in the creation and development of the museum. This internship is designed to provide hands-on experience in oral history, archival preservation, museum operations, and board relations while developing professional communication, research, and project management skills. Through participation in the Council Oral History Project, the intern will gain practical experience supporting the collection, preservation, and interpretation of historical narratives within a museum setting. The intern will develop a greater understanding of how culturally specific museums operate and how oral history programs support exhibitions, research, collections, and public engagement. Through direct involvement with the Oral History Initiative and Council Relations and Museum Initiatives team, the intern will learn how oral history projects are planned, managed, and implemented from concept through accession into a museum collection.As part of the project, the intern will gain professional experience in archival and oral history practices while supporting the preparation and management of oral history interviews and records. Responsibilities may include archiving Council meeting materials, conducting background research on interview subjects, collecting and organizing oral history documentation, reviewing and proofreading transcripts, writing interview summaries and field notes, preparing collections documentation, observing oral history interviews, and assisting with the planning and implementation of public programs. Key learning objectives include:Developing oral history research and documentation skills through conducting background research, gathering metadata, maintaining records, and supporting interview preparation; Learning archival and digital preservation practices, including transcript review, file management, documentation collection, and preservation workflows; Building professional writing and communication skills by preparing interview summaries, field notes, collections justifications, and other project documentation; Gaining an understanding of board and donor relations through exposure to the museum’s Advisory Council and the Founding Council Oral History Project; Learning ethical standards and best practices in oral history collection as established by the Oral History Association;Developing knowledge of museum collections management and the process of bringing materials into a museum collection;Observing and participating in oral history interviews, including interview preparation, documentation, and post-interview processing;Understanding how oral history content is integrated into museum exhibitions, public programs, and educational initiatives.The internship provides hands-on opportunities through active participation in staff meetings, informational interviews with Smithsonian staff and leadership, oral history documentation, transcript processing, archival research, and public programming support. These experiences allow the intern to apply classroom knowledge in a professional museum environment while developing transferable skills in research, project coordination, records management, writing, digital preservation, and stakeholder engagement. These competencies are highly valuable within the museum field and are also transferable to careers in archives, libraries, public history, cultural heritage organizations, nonprofit management, research institutions, education, communications, and project management. The internship equips participants with both specialized museum knowledge and broadly applicable professional skills that support success across a wide range of industries.This project is important because it preserves the firsthand accounts of the leaders whose vision, advocacy, fundraising efforts, and strategic guidance helped establish NMAAHC. Their experiences provide unique insight into the museum’s creation, from the early efforts to establish the museum through site selection, fundraising, and the museum’s opening. By documenting and preserving these stories, the project ensures that an important part of the museum’s institutional history is available to future researchers, museum professionals, and the public. The internship directly supports the work of both the Council Relations and Museum Initiatives team and the Oral History Initiative. The Council Relations and Museum Initiatives team is responsible for managing the museum’s Advisory Council and advancing museum-wide initiatives, while the Oral History Initiative works to document, preserve, and interpret African American stories through oral history projects that support research, exhibitions, programming, and public engagement. The project aligns closely with NMAAHC’s mission by contributing to the preservation, documentation, and dissemination of African American history and culture. Through oral history collection, archival preservation, and public access initiatives, the project helps ensure that the stories of individuals who shaped the museum and contributed to its success are preserved and shared with diverse audiences for generations to come.The ideal candidate will have a strong interest in oral history, historical research, archives, museum operations, and the preservation and interpretation of African American history and culture. The internship is particularly valuable for students seeking careers in museums, archives, libraries, cultural institutions, public history organizations, and related nonprofit or educational sectors. Preferred qualifications include:Demonstrated interest in oral history interviews and oral history methodology;Interest in African American history, cultural studies, the history of philanthropy, and culturally specific museum leadership; Interest in systems thinking, workflows, and process improvement; Strong organizational skills and attention to detail;Ability to work independently and manage self-directed assignments;Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively both independently and in collaborative team environments.Desired technical and professional competencies include experience or interest in conducting research, reviewing and proofreading written materials, maintaining records and documentation, managing digital files, and supporting archival or oral history projects. Familiarity with Microsoft Office applications, digital collaboration tools, and database or records management systems is beneficial but not required. The selected intern will support the Council Oral History Project through a combination of daily responsibilities, short-term assignments, and long-term projects that provide practical experience in oral history, archival preservation, museum operations, and research. These duties are designed to help the intern achieve the learning objectives of the internship while contributing to the preservation of NMAAHC's institutional history. These responsibilities provide the intern with progressive, hands-on experience in oral history methodology, archival management, research, professional writing, digital preservation, and museum operations while contributing to a project that preserves the stories of the leaders who helped shape the National Museum of African American History and Culture.Internship Duties Include (but are not limited to):Attend staff meetings and mandatory training sessionsParticipate in informational interviews with Smithsonian staff and museum leadershipConduct background research on interview subjects and topics related to oral history projectsCollect, organize, and maintain oral history documentation and project records Review, reformat, proofread, and process oral history transcripts Write interview summaries, field notes, and supporting project documentation Observe oral history interviews and assist with interview preparation and follow-up activitiesSupport the planning and implementation of public programs related to oral history initiativesSupport the archiving and organization of historical Council meeting records for the Council Oral History Project Assist in documenting and preserving oral histories of Council members and other project participants Prepare and compile background research materials that support oral history interviews and project development Assist with metadata collection, records management, and digital preservation activities associated with oral history collections. Draft justifications and supporting documentation for collections-related review processesContribute to ongoing oral history project workflows from interview planning and documentation through transcript processing and archival preparationSupport efforts to make oral history materials accessible for future research, exhibitions, programming, and public engagement

jobs.description: Employer: Skipper AI Expires: 10/10/2026 Brand Insights Intern Position Title: Brand Insights InternTarget Start Date: September 28, 2026Department: MarketingHours per Week: 5-12 hrsDuration: 6 MonthsApplication Deadline: September 21, 2026Immediate Supervisor: James LuceySupervisor Title: Chief Operating OfficerCompensation: HourlyRange: $15-$20 an hour, based on experience. Position summaryThe Brand Insights Intern at Skipper AI turns real information and stories into content that builds the Skipper brand. You're a creative writer at heart, motivated to represent Skipper AI's brand voice and pursue projects across marketing and content that bring that voice to life. You'll manage your own schedule and project-manage your own work, coordinating effectively with internal stakeholders and, where relevant, external ones as well. At the center of the role is a simple skill: taking raw information and turning it into insights and stories that align with where Skipper's brand and marketing are headed. This is a role for someone who wants their creativity to shape how a real company is seen. Success factorsManages their own schedule and workload while staying in sync with internal stakeholders.Comfortable turning raw information into a clear, compelling narrative.Genuinely curious and observant, picks up on details worth turning into a story.Organized enough to track multiple ideas and projects at different stages at once.Strongly represents Skipper AI's brand voice across everything they create. Required qualifications | Position competencies & skillsComfortable with ambiguity and figuring out the best approach for an idea.Organized and disciplined enough to track multiple ideas and projects simultaneously without losing the thread.Self-directed and accountable, takes ownership of their work and pursues critiques with a positive growth mindset.Quick to pick up new tools, will be onboarded on Jira, Confluence, and the platforms Skipper AI uses.Comfortable in an early-stage environment where priorities shift and not everything is defined yet. Preferred qualificationsHas independently started and carried a creative project through to completion, a blog, content series, or channel of their own.Experience with content or design tools, comfortable figuring things out without step-by- step guidance.Interest in marketing, branding, or storytelling for a business.Interest in video, design, or other creative mediums beyond writing.Curiosity about how brands build trust and reputation over time. Position responsibilitiesContent creation Create approved content in various formats, written, visual, video, or otherwise.Maintain Skipper AI's brand voice across everything you contribute to.Pursue projects with the expectation of iterating through drafts, incorporating feedback, and refining work through to final approval.Track the impact published pieces have on the company. Idea development and pitching Turn raw information and observations into content pitches.Collaborate with Skipper AI leadership and stakeholders to prioritize relevant projects while maintaining a backlog of ideas for later.Log and track pitches through the approval process, from idea to in- progress to published. Internal communication and check-ins Join regular check-ins with internal stakeholders to stay aligned on priorities and ideas.Write up takeaways and actionable items from meetings and conversations.Communicate proactively on scheduling conflicts, blockers, or shifts in priority. What you will gainA real portfolio of published creative work.Direct access to leadership and how brand decisions actually get made.Hands-on experience turning raw ideas into finished, public-facing content.A front-row seat to how a young AI consultancy builds its brand from the ground up.Practice pitching and defending your own creative ideas in a real business setting.Trackable KPIs and outcomes from the content you contribute to. Work designationThis position is fully remote. All core responsibilities are performed independently and do not require a fixed on-site schedule.The team looks for opportunities to meet in person when project timelines and individual schedules align. These gatherings are intentional but informal, driven by shared momentum rather than a fixed cadence. Skipper AI core valuesTrust and Transparency. We communicate openly, follow through on commitments, and treat every client and colleague with honesty. Trust is the foundation of every relationship we build. Humble Hunger. There's more to a failed task than the task itself; every mistake carries a lesson, and progress in anything is still progress forward. It's okay to be wrong, as long as you admit it. What matters is being hungry more often than you are wrong. Have Hard Conversations. One's success in life is directly correlated to their ability to have hard conversations. Conversations are hard if you are passionate, and two passionate people in a room is a rare thing. About Skipper AIIn the last year, we have worked with 8 companies, on countless projects, and have shipped things that did and didn't work. Importantly, we have captured the themes behind what leads to success or failure, and have not found a use case since those learnings did not apply. Skipper AI exists to not skip them. We've driven 90%+ adoption not because of the platform we picked, but because we refuse to skip the intentional steps. Intentionality through change has never been more important. The tools are the easy part; it's the steps most firms rush past, the change management in between where AI actually sticks or quietly dies.

Responsibilities Throughout the summer, you will be exposed to:Project Management: Working in project management gives you an understanding of the day-to-day and long-term business and financial management associated with construction projects.Financial Management - Review gross billings, track change orders, and subcontractor requisitions Document Control - Manage the submittals, RFI, and material tracking process Trade Partner Success - Become a trusted advisor to our subcontractors to plan for a successful field installationField Management: Learn the intricacies of the building process, assist in site logistics, and ensure quality and safety on our jobsites.Quality Control and Safety - Monitor tradeworkers with emphasis on the quality of work and safetyProject Schedule - Assist with schedule management and site logistics Critical Thinking - Resolve unforeseen challenges within installation, schedule, and trade partner coordinationProject Development: Understand how we acquire new work, develop winning strategies, and build strong client relationships through budgeting, estimating, and purchasingBudgeting - Review initial contract documents, solicit, and provide preliminary evaluations of subcontractor bidsEstimating - Perform quantity takeoffs, prepare the overall bid proposal, and quantify labor and material prices required for projects Purchasing - Collaborate to execute subcontractor agreements, review the scope of work, and manage relationships with subcontractorsBusiness Operations: Explore the essential functions that keep our company running smoothly, gaining a holistic view of the Clark organization. Basic QualificationsPursuing an undergraduate degree or equivalent, or a graduate degreeInterest and passion for the construction industry What a Successful Candidate Looks LikeWe look for individuals who embody these core principles:Enthusiasm & Drive: Be punctual and dedicated, staying until work is done. Arrive early for meetings and events. Be a proactive team player – ask how you can help and be present. Take initiative, represent the company professionally (dress, demeanor), and build trust with your team, clients, and stakeholders. Proactively seek ways to contribute to team success, and always maintain a positive attitude.Delivery & Performance: Reliably meet the expectations of your role and commitments. Understand and follow Clark's standard procedures. Take on new responsibilities, dig into the details, and bring solutions to problems. Take ownership, be accountable, and demonstrate responsiveness with a sense of urgency.Learning & Growth: Immerse yourself in Clark's culture, your team, and your community. Fulfill Clark Corporate University learning requirements. Be engaged, accountable, and self-directed in your learning – be curious! Continuously build your technical expertise and grow your business acumen. The work environment and requirements described below are representative of those necessary for an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this role. The Physical Side of the Role: This is an active, hands-on role. You can expect to be on your feet frequently, navigating active job sites with uneven terrain, stairs, ladders, and hoists. The work is physically demanding and requires a full range of motion, including bending, kneeling, and reaching. You’ll need to be comfortable frequently lifting and carrying materials up to 25 pounds, and occasionally up to 50 pounds. This role requires the ability to communicate effectively, as well as visual acuity for reading plans and inspecting work. The role does include desk time in the office that may require prolonged periods of sitting for tasks like computer work, document review, and meetings.Your Work Environment: You’ll spend a significant amount of your time on active construction sites, which means being adaptable to all kinds of weather and moderate to loud noise levels, and comfortable in elevated or confined work areas with moving mechanical equipment and with the fast-paced nature of a project in progress. You will also spend time in a typical office setting with moderate noise levels. Your safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to follow Clark Construction's safety policies and procedures, and all applicable laws, at all locations.Our High-Performing Culture: This is a demanding, high-performance environment. We are looking for candidates who are energized by challenge, thrive under pressure, and are prepared to do what it takes to achieve exceptional results. Success in this role requires significant commitment, including flexibility to work extended hours, especially during critical project phases or client deadlines.A Drug Free Workplace: Clark promotes a drug free workplace. A pre-employment fitness for duty screening is required, and random fitness for duty tests of employees are conducted quarterly.

jobs.feedName: Mike Curb College of Arts, Media, & Communication
jobs.title: Graphic Design Intern at Marketing for Change
jobs.description: Employer: Marketing for Change Expires: 10/11/2026 The Change Academy at Marketing for Change offers graduate students, college seniors, recent graduates and other emerging creatives a paid semester-long experience working and learning at one of the nation’s leading behavior-change marketing agencies. In behavior-change marketing, the objective is not sales or profits; it’s influencing behaviors in a way that leads to a healthier, safer, more sustainable world. We’re looking for a Graphic Design & Creative Intern who wants to put their creative skills to work on real projects with real impact. You’ll work alongside our creative team and other experts across the agency, gaining hands-on experience developing visual concepts and creative work for campaigns designed to make a difference. As part of the Change Academy, you’ll have opportunities to contribute to real client work while strengthening your design skills and learning how behavioral science informs creative strategy. Depending on the project, your work may include graphic design, visual concepting, campaign creative, digital and social content, presentation design, and other visual storytelling. You’ll receive mentorship and skill-specific training from experienced creatives, along with broader training in behavioral science and behavior-change marketing. You’ll also participate in agency events, client meetings and, if you want, off-the-clock social gatherings. Interns earn $18.40 an hour or minimum wage (whichever is higher) and work 20 hours a week, with at least one day a week in our offices. The in-office experience is critical to helping interns improve their skills, work directly with mentors and share a group experience with their cohort. Please confirm you can participate in person at your selected location. LocationOur work hubs are located in Orlando and just outside Washington, DC, and we very much prefer to hire people willing to locate in those areas. We are mostly a hybrid workforce with staff working together in-person at least one day a week because we value the fun and collaboration that allows. The program lasts between 12 and 16 weeks depending on the semester. Instruction takes place during the first 6 to 8 weeks of the internship, mixed with group projects and real work experience. The final weeks focus on work experience and give interns an opportunity to build their portfolios with meaningful, professional creative experience. The Change Academy is the main path to entry-level employment at Marketing for Change. Several former M4C interns are now in leadership roles at M4C, including an art director, creative director, senior media planner and strategist. What we’re looking for:Relevant experience, coursework or training in graphic design, visual communication, advertising, art direction or a related creative field. Preference is given to graduate students, recent graduates or college seniors with at least one prior internship or comparable creative experience. Other adults with the right skills but no degree may also apply. Several have been successful in the past.A portfolio or work samples that show your design skills, creative thinking and visual point of view. School, internship, freelance and personal projects are all welcome.Familiarity with common design tools and an interest in continuing to build your creative and technical skills.A willingness to take feedback, try new ideas and collaborate with other creatives, strategists and agency teams.Deep curiosity about what makes people tick and how design can influence what people notice, feel and do.An interest in using your creative powers for good and making the world a better place.Being a nice person. Seriously. We want the kind of person most other people love to work with. A quick note about our hiring processApplying for a job can feel a little like sending your application out into the void and hoping a real person is on the other side. At Marketing for Change, one will be. Real people on our team review every application. We may use technology to make parts of the process easier, but when it comes to getting to know you, considering what you could bring to our team and making hiring decisions, that’s us. We know there’s a real person on the other side of every application, too. Someone who gave us their time, shared a little bit of their story and decided we might be worth exploring. We don’t take that lightly. And if you’re considering us, we’re genuinely glad you’re here. Note: Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and Form I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification. TimingSeptember 2026 to January 2027
